binders: An arbitrary scalar space-time field q and arbitrary real speed,x,t.
hypotheses: At (x,t), q has time and space derivatives satisfying q_t+speed*q_x=0.
conclusions: The one-component embedding Q satisfies the conservative residual Q_t + d/dx(F(Q))=0 at (x,t) for F(U)=[speed]U.
For every one-component state U, [speed]U is the function whose sole component is speed*U(0).
mathematical_definitions: The conservative predicate differentiates the composed spatial function x -> F(Q(x,t)).
translation.proposition_plain_english: A pointwise scalar advection residual implies the corresponding one-component conservative residual for the linear flux F(U)=[speed]U, and the theorem also identifies that matrix flux componentwise as speed times the unique state component.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: This is a one-way implication, not an equivalence.
It is restricted to one real component and a constant linear flux.
The premise is only a pointwise residual predicate and does not assert global differentiability or a global solution.
No sign condition on speed, initial data, boundary data, or uniqueness is encoded.
